requirement: comment-only content is reported as unknown, not confidently attributed to a vendor
input: two '!' comment lines and nothing else
evidence: E03 F7: syntax-aware comment-only check — '!' is Cisco's comment marker; FortiOS '#' and JUNOS '##' are live syntax and are never stripped. Pre-fix this input returned cisco with conf>=0.55 (recorded as PARTIAL)

requirement: an unsupported vendor's configuration is reported as unknown
input: Arista-style EOS config (not in the 4 supported vendors)
expected: vendor=unknown (spec: 'We don't claim to support every vendor')
actual: vendor=cisco platform=ios conf=0.635 path=ml dt=router host=spine1 — shared IOS/EOS syntax, no EOS-specific pattern exists; verdict is stable
evidence: detection.py has no EOS patterns; router/interface/switchport are shared with Cisco so both paths said cisco pre- and post-fix. The executor gate (E03 F2) only stops vendors detection names as out-of-scope
recommendation: Add vendor-specific patterns (EOS: mlag/daemon/management api) or a calibrated low-margin fallback — deferred, not E03-blocking

requirement: one attacker-supplied line must not be sufficient to reassign vendor
input: 3 IOS lines, then the same 3 lines + one line containing 'Palo Alto'
evidence: E03 F1 fix: a banner-only line is below MIN_EVIDENCE_PATTERNS and has no structural evidence, so it can never beat the IOS structural score. Pre-fix a single injected 'Palo Alto' line scored 3.0 and flipped both paths (detection.py:222-225 banner re.search over every line)
recommendation: Evidence hierarchy enforced in _decide(): structural beats banner; banner-only is ineligible

requirement: banner text inside a comment line cannot claim its vendor
input: '!' comment line containing 'Juniper Networks' + an IOS hostname
expected: vendor must not be juniper — comment content is not device identity (cisco structural evidence here is only 1 distinct pattern, so the verdict is unknown)
evidence: E03 F1/F7 fix: juniper's banner is banner-only (no structural match), and cisco's only match ('^!' comment + hostname with no digit) is below MIN_EVIDENCE_PATTERNS=2 — both ineligible, verdict unknown. Pre-fix the juniper banner scored 3.0 and won (detection.py:222-225)

requirement: evidence text is echoed from the configuration verbatim
expected: evidence matched_text is taken from the config (documented here as a display/injection consideration for reports)
actual: matched_text='! Cisco IOS Software, C2960 Software' (truncated to 100 chars at detection.py:327)
evidence: detection.py:327 line.strip()[:100] is stored and later rendered by reporting.py — any report consumer must treat it as untrusted data
recommendation: Escape evidence text before HTML/PDF rendering (reporting layer)

requirement: a 5000-line banner flood cannot inflate confidence past the cap or exhaust memory with evidence
regex scoring completes on a large input (no super-linear blow-up)
evidence: every pattern is scanned against every line (26 patterns x N lines) — cost is linear in lines but with a large constant

requirement: API-level detection runs on the same full content the audit pipeline detects on (no truncation)
expected: no [:6000]/[:4000] slicing of raw_content before detect(); the three VendorDetector call sites remain
evidence: E03 F4: detect() receives raw_content directly at all three sites (pre-fix :137/[:6000], :178/[:4000], :215/[:6000] — the same file could publish 'unknown' live while the audit said 'cisco', see V03-59)

requirement: detection is a pure, stable function of the full content every call site now passes; a bare prefix is a different input
input: 53003 chars vs the same file truncated to 6000 chars (the prefix row is informational only)
expected: identical vendor/platform/confidence/evidence for identical full content
actual: full=cisco/ios/0.660 again=cisco/0.660 [:6000]=unknown/unknown (different input, callers no longer truncate — V03-58)
evidence: E03 F4/F17: callers pass full content and detection runs once per audit (V03-72); pre-fix the API truncated to 6000 chars and could publish 'unknown' while the audit published 'cisco' for the same file

requirement: the 10-item evidence cap holds on the ML path too
input: ML forced confident + 1 FortiOS structural line + 20 banner-matching lines
expected: <= 10 evidence items, ML marker first, path=ml
evidence: E03 F11 fix: collect evidence -> insert the ML marker -> cap at 10. Pre-fix the cap ran inside _collect_evidence and the marker was inserted afterwards, so an ML result could carry 11 items (observed on the corpus for Juniper/Firewalls/SRX/configs_junos-srx-1.cfg)

input: cisco config + injected Palo Alto line; Juniper comment + hostname; cisco banner + hostname (regex path)
evidence: detection.py _decide(): MIN_EVIDENCE_PATTERNS=2 distinct patterns AND structural > 0 required; banner-only vendors are ineligible. Pre-fix a single banner line scored 3.0 and flipped the verdict (V03-42/V03-43)
